observations: The page number «( 4 )» stands at the head of the page, centred. The page has no signature.

L01: the two groups of four points, after «hec» and after «.xx», mark the places of the figures of ten and twenty, which the edition does not print; the footnote says that both gaps are in the manuscript too, at fol. 102 verso, line 33. «.xx» has no closing point before the second gap; «(1).Et» is printed without a space after the point (a gap of 6 px, where the word spaces of the line are 14 to 26 px). The vertical bar between «ita,» and «et» marks the beginning of fol. 103 recto of the manuscript, which the note in the left margin, «car. 103 recto.», names; transcribed as a margin note.

L06, L07: the numerals of the fourth place, the thousands, are printed with a bar over the small capitals: «.ī.», 1000, and «.īī.», 2000, the bar running over both letters. L17: «.īx̄.», 9000, with a bar over «.ix» that begins above the first point. L20: «ix.» is printed without the opening point.

L12-L19: the figures of the hundreds and thousands are printed with old-style arabic numerals: «.100.» (L12), «.300.» (L13, L15), «.1000» (L18) and «2000» (L19). L13: the figure of two hundred, «figura ducentorum … sicut figura duorum posita … in tercia differentia», is printed «.300.», the figure that L14-L15 give for three hundred; see the critical note. L15: «.300,» has no closing point. L18: «.1000:» has no closing point. L19: «ita. 2000.»: the point stands after «ita», and a word space before «2000».

L29: «.ii.», in small capitals like the roman numerals of the line, for the number eleven written with figures; the old-style figure 1 of «.1000» (L18) has a flag at its top left, and the two letters of «.ii.» the serifs of the small capital I of «.xi».
L09: «sequitur sequitur (sic)»: the edition prints the word twice and marks the repetition with «(sic)» in italics.

Spaces at punctuation (rule of tools/punct.py: after a mark, a space where the gap is at least 12 px or two thirds of the median word space of the line; before a mark, where it is at least 10 px): before the mark, L02 «.ix. :» (23 px), L04 «est ,» (11 px), L07 «.xx. ,» and «.cc. ,» (19 px), L28 «gratia :» (14 px), L29 «eum ,» (20 px) and «.ii. :» (23 px). L13 «.300.:figura»: the point, the colon and the word follow each other with gaps of 7 px, without spaces (the median word space of the line 13 px). L12 «.100.;»: 8 px between the point and the semicolon, without a space.
copy_matter: A reader's notes in pencil: L04 and L06, «sic» underlined, and «significat» written in the left margin beside L04, a gloss of «sic»; L05, a hook under the first «e» of «tercia»; L06 and L07, strokes around «.ī.» and «.īī.»; L13, a stroke under «.300.» and «200» written in the left margin beside the line; beside L15-L16 in the left margin, «. nongentos . Hanc», a reading of «nongenta. Hac» (L15); L16, a stroke over «li» of «similiter»; L22, a faint mark above «unius». Not part of the edition.

critical_notes.evidence: the sentence gives the figure of two hundred as the figure of two placed in the third place («figura ducentorum est sicut figura duorum posita similiter in tercia differentia ita»), which is 200; the edition prints .300., the figure that the next sentence gives for three hundred («figura … tercentorum est figura trium … ita .300», L14-L15), after .100. for one hundred (L12); a reader of this copy wrote «200» in the margin beside the line
critical_notes.impact: the example of two hundred reads 200; whether the error is of the edition or of the manuscript is not shown by the print
